scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: An IT Department user (it_hod, 192.168.1.2) reports they
cannot reach CS Department hosts (192.168.2.0/24) -- inter-department routing
between IT and CS seems broken. They suspect router0 (which connects both
segments) dropped one of its department interfaces or a static/RIP entry. Please
confirm the inter-department fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Inter-department Layer-3 connectivity between the IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS (192.168.2.0/24) segments is functioning normally. Router0, which interconnects both departments, has both department-facing interfaces up and correctly addressed (eth0=192.168.1.1/24, eth1=192.168.2.1/24). Its routing table includes directly connected routes for 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24, so no dynamic/static entry is required for inter-department traffic.

Mechanism verification: From the reporting host it_hod (192.168.1.2), ICMP to multiple CS hosts succeeds with 0% loss and ~1 ms RTT: cs_hod (192.168.2.2), cs_lab1 (192.168.2.3), cs_lab2 (192.168.2.4), cs_lab3 (192.168.2.5), cs_lab4 (192.168.2.6). Reverse direction is also healthy (cs_hod -> it_hod, 0% loss). Host default gateways are correct (it_hod via 192.168.1.1; cs_hod via 192.168.2.1), ensuring proper return path. Router0’s interfaces eth0/eth1 report UP/RUNNING, further ruling out an interface drop.

Localization: No fault localized; router0, IT and CS hosts all show expected interface and routing states.

Root cause: No current fault was found—routing and interfaces on router0 are correct, and end-to-end IT↔CS connectivity is verified; the reported outage is not reproducible.

Corrective fix: None required. If the user experienced a transient issue, consider monitoring switch port/link state and ARP/ICMP reachability, and verify host firewalls if problems recur. Please have the user re-test; connectivity is currently good.
